testSuites.title: Test Suites
testSuites.subtitle: Manage your automated test suites
testSuites.noneYetNoCreate: No test suites yet. Ask an admin to add you to one.
testSuites.httpProxyHint: Proxy used by Playwright when running tests. Leave empty for direct connection. Per-domain proxy rules can be added after creating the suite, from Edit Suite.
testSuites.historyHint: Older runs (and their screenshots) are deleted automatically per test.
testSuites.confirmDuplicateSuite: Duplicate suite "{name}"? A new suite will be created and all tests will be copied in the background.

testSuiteShow.searchTestsPlaceholder: Search tests by name or description...
testSuiteShow.noneYet: No tests yet. Add your first test.
testSuiteShow.webhookInstructions: POST to this URL from CI (e.g. GitHub Actions) to trigger a run of this suite.
testSuiteShow.testIdsHint: Pass test_ids as a query parameter (e.g. ?test_ids=1,2,3) to run only specific tests; omit it to run every active test in the suite.
testSuiteShow.noScheduleConfigured: No schedule configured. Add a crontab expression to run this suite automatically.
testSuiteShow.defaultProxyHint: Used for any request that doesn't match a per-host rule below. Leave empty for direct connection.
testSuiteShow.perHostProxyHint: Routes requests through a specific proxy when the hostname matches a regular expression, overriding the default above. Checked on every request, including each hop of a redirect chain.
testSuiteShow.proxyRulesInfoIntro: Each rule's domain is a regular expression tested against the request's hostname (case-insensitive), checked on every request including each hop of a redirect chain.
testSuiteShow.proxyRulesExactHost: Exact host only — matches example.com, not foo.example.com
testSuiteShow.proxyRulesHostOrSubdomain: Host or any subdomain — matches example.com and foo.example.com, but not notexample.com
testSuiteShow.proxyRulesAvoid: Avoid — unanchored at the start, so it also matches unrelated hosts like notexample.com
testSuiteShow.noRulesConfigured: No rules configured — all requests use the default proxy above (or connect directly).
testSuiteShow.variablesHint: Key/value pairs injected into every test run as a `variables` object in the Playwright code scope. Reference them in test code as variables.KEY. Useful for credentials or environment-specific values that should not be hardcoded in test code.
testSuiteShow.noVariablesConfigured: No variables configured — add one to make it available in test code as variables.KEY.
testSuiteShow.cookiesHint: Cookies added to the browser context before any page is created, so tests start already authenticated. Each cookie must set either a domain or a URL.
testSuiteShow.noCookiesConfigured: No cookies configured — add one or paste a cookie JSON to inject it at the start of every test run.
testSuiteShow.pasteCookieJsonHint: Paste a Playwright cookie array or a storageState JSON object. Existing cookies with the same name+domain+path will be replaced; new ones will be added.
testSuiteShow.pasteCookieJsonError: Could not parse JSON. Please check the format.
testSuiteShow.historyHint: Older runs (and their screenshots) are deleted automatically per test.
testSuiteShow.msTeamsWebhookHint: Incoming webhook or workflow URL for a Teams channel. Leave empty to disable.
testSuiteShow.msTeamsWebhookProxyHint: Optional proxy used only for the Teams webhook call. Independent of the HTTP Proxy above. Leave empty for direct connection.
testSuiteShow.integrationsHint: Hooks that run before and/or after each run. GitHub Actions workflows are dispatched using the Sorify GitHub App installation token; HTTP request integrations call a URL with GET/POST/PUT/DELETE. A 'before' hook must complete successfully for the run's tests to start.
testSuiteShow.noIntegrations: No integrations configured — add a GitHub Action or HTTP request to trigger before or after runs.
testSuiteShow.githubActionsNotConfigured: No GitHub App is configured for workflow dispatch. Add one under Admin → GitHub Apps (with its App ID and private key), and install it on the target repository.
testSuiteShow.integrationGithubAppHint: Which GitHub App (public GitHub or a GitHub Enterprise instance) to dispatch the workflow as.
testSuiteShow.httpBodyHint: Sent as-is with POST / PUT. When set, inputs become query parameters.
testSuiteShow.sorifyContextHint: Injected into every dispatch automatically — reserved, not editable. The status/counts are only filled on "after run" dispatches.
testSuiteShow.httpInputsHintGet: GET: inputs are appended as query parameters and take priority over same-named URL parameters.
testSuiteShow.httpInputsHintBody: POST / PUT / DELETE: inputs are sent as an application/json body; URL query parameters are kept.
testSuiteShow.triggerBeforeHint: Run before the run starts and wait for it to complete. Tests only run when it succeeds.
testSuiteShow.triggerAfterHint: Run after the run completes, with the run result passed as context (sorify_run_status, counts, etc.).
testSuiteShow.crontabHint: Standard 5-field crontab syntax (minute hour day month weekday), e.g. '0 */6 * * *' runs every 6 hours.
testSuiteShow.allUsersHaveAccess: All users already have access to this suite.
testSuiteShow.viewOnlyEditTitle: This user is view-only; edit is unavailable.
testSuiteShow.viewOnlyDeleteTitle: This user is view-only; delete is unavailable.
testSuiteShow.viewOnlyRunTitle: This user is view-only; run is unavailable.
testSuiteShow.noUsersAdded: No users have been added yet.
testSuiteShow.confirmRegenerateWebhook: This will generate a new webhook URL. The old URL stays active until you delete it, so existing CI configurations keep working. Continue?
testSuiteShow.confirmDeleteWebhook: Delete this old webhook URL? Any CI configuration still using it will stop working.
testSuiteShow.oldWebhookUrlsHint: These URLs are still active. Delete the ones you no longer use — you must delete old URLs before generating new ones once the limit is reached.
testSuiteShow.webhookLimitReached: Webhook limit reached (5). Delete an old webhook URL to generate a new one.
testSuiteShow.confirmRemoveSchedule: Remove the schedule for this suite? It will no longer run automatically.
testSuiteShow.confirmDeleteTests: Delete {count} test(s)? This cannot be undone.
testSuiteShow.confirmDeleteSuite: Delete suite "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
testSuiteShow.reviewAllTestsTitle: Open a pull-request-style page to review every test's Playwright code in one go
testSuiteShow.confirmDuplicateSuite: Duplicate suite "{name}"? A new suite will be created and all tests will be copied in the background.
testSuiteShow.duplicationInProgressBody: Tests from the source suite are being copied in the background. This page refreshes automatically every few seconds — new tests will appear here as they land.
testSuiteShow.duplicationFailed: Duplication failed — some tests may not have been copied. Check the suite and try again if needed.
testSuiteShow.confirmDuplicateTest: Duplicate test "{name}"? A copy will be created in this suite.

adminGithubApps.heading: GitHub Apps
adminGithubApps.intro: Configured GitHub Apps for sign-in and Actions dispatch — public GitHub and/or GitHub Enterprise instances. github ids are only unique per app, so users and integrations remember which app they belong to.
adminGithubApps.name: Name
adminGithubApps.appIdPlaceholder: Numeric App ID, e.g. 337 — only needed for workflow dispatch
adminGithubApps.privateKeyHint: Paste the app's .pem as a \n-escaped one-liner — run awk with printf "%s\\n" on the .pem and copy the output.
adminGithubApps.clientSecretPlaceholder: The app's client secret (Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps)
adminGithubApps.redirectUriPlaceholder: Optional — overrides the default callback URL
adminGithubApps.secretStoredPlaceholder: ●●●●●●●●●●●● — leave blank to keep the stored secret
adminGithubApps.secretNotSetPlaceholder: Not set yet — paste to store
adminGithubApps.confirmDelete: Delete the GitHub App "{name}"? Users who signed in with it keep their accounts but lose GitHub sign-in; its integrations fall back to the default app.
adminGithubApps.proxyHint: Used for all outbound traffic to this GitHub instance: the sign-in OAuth calls and, by default, its GitHub Action integrations.
adminGithubApps.signInSwitchHint: Show a "Sign in with {name}" button on the login and signup pages
adminGithubApps.actionsSwitchHint: Allow GitHub Action integrations to dispatch as this app
adminGithubApps.step1Detail: Settings (org or personal) → Developer Settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App.
adminGithubApps.homepageUrlValue: Your Sorify URL (the address you use to open this dashboard).
adminGithubApps.step3Note: Everything else stays at No access.
adminGithubApps.step4Detail: Settings (org or personal) → Developer Settings → GitHub Apps → click the app → Install App → choose the destination.
adminGithubApps.step5Detail: Admin → GitHub Apps → Add GitHub App, then paste the Client ID, Client Secret — and for workflow dispatch the App ID and private key — into the form.
adminGithubApps.workflowNote: Sorify injects the sorify_* inputs — do not edit them. Add custom inputs from the suite's settings page.
adminGithubApps.connectionSkipped: Enter a valid http(s) base URL to test the connection
